review_notes: I read all 88 lines of the target file and inspected every declaration: `distanceDifferenceKernel` (lines 10–11) and its measurability lemma (13–15), `fourPairGood` (17–18) and its measurability lemma (20–22), `enorm_setIntegral_le_good_kernel` (24–41), and `original_complex_kernel_max` (45–82, with a local `let T`/`he` at 72–78). For the two definitions that could in principle compete with a library concept, I grepped Mathlib for `distanceDifference`, for kernels of the form `1/(1 + ... |dist · · - dist · ·|)^2`, and for `def ...Kernel` declarations: Mathlib contains only unrelated kernels (`Probability.Kernel`, `poissonKernel`, `cartanKernel`, reproducing-kernel `kernel`, `oddKernel`/`sinKernel`, etc.), and its only occurrences of `|dist a c - dist b c|` are generic metric lemmas such as `abs_dist_sub_le`, not a named collision/distance-difference kernel. `fourPairGood` is merely the product-preimage set of the measurable equivalence and has no Mathlib counterpart. The remaining results are theorems, which the rubric excludes (standalone theorem duplication/proof shortening). One observation outside the rubric's scope, recorded for transparency but not reported as a finding: the same closed formula appears in a sibling project file as `distanceCollisionKernelND` (`OAI/MeasureTheory/FalconerCompletion/Measures/DistanceCollisionKernel.lean:22-23`, real-valued on `(V×V)×(V×V)`), but that is another file of the same project, not a Mathlib/core/Batteries concept, so it does not satisfy this rubric's criterion. Remaining uncertainty: I could not run Lean, so I verified only the definitions' source text and their documented uses, not compiled statements; this does not affect the conclusion that neither new definition has a Mathlib analogue.
